title: A. Tokitsukaze and Strange Inequality
statement:
Tokitsukaze has a permutation p of length n. Recall that a permutation p of length n is a sequence p_1, p_2, …, p_n consisting of n distinct integers, each of which from 1 to n (1 ≤ p_i ≤ n).

She wants to know how many different indices tuples [a,b,c,d] (1 ≤ a < b < c < d ≤ n) in this permutation satisfy the following two inequalities:

Note that two tuples [a_1,b_1,c_1,d_1] and [a_2,b_2,c_2,d_2] are considered to be different if a_1 ≠ a_2 or b_1 ≠ b_2 or c_1 ≠ c_2 or d_1 ≠ d_2.

The first line contains one integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) — the number of test cases. Each test case consists of two lines.

The first line contains a single integer n (4 ≤ n ≤ 5000) — the length of permutation p.

The second line contains n integers p_1, p_2, …, p_n (1 ≤ p_i ≤ n) — the permutation p.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 5000.

For each test case, print a single integer — the number of different [a,b,c,d] tuples.

In the first test case, there are 3 different [a,b,c,d] tuples.

p_1 = 5, p_2 = 3, p_3 = 6, p_4 = 1, where p_1 < p_3 and p_2 > p_4 satisfies the inequality, so one of [a,b,c,d] tuples is [1,2,3,4].

Similarly, other two tuples are [1,2,3,6], [2,3,5,6].

Input:
```
365 3 6 1 4 241 2 3 4105 1 6 2 8 3 4 10 9 7
```

Output:
```
3
0
28
```
